title: A Typewriter for the Letter
premise: In the winter of 1899, apprentice clockmaker Elodie Whitlock is sent to the remote mountain town of Verenchal to repair the observatory's failing master clock, only to find the bridge closed by flood and herself stranded among strangers. She uncovers a decades-old cover-up: the town's founding families drowned a rival settlement's claim to the valley and erased its people from the record, and the observatory itself was built on their stolen land. As the town's victors prepare a centennial history to seal the lie forever, Elodie — with a retired postmistress, a disgraced schoolteacher, and the clockmaker's estranged daughter — races to document the truth using an old typewriter and the observatory's own archive. The master clock, repaired at last, becomes the instrument that broadcasts their testimony as the century turns, forcing the town to choose between its comfortable myth and a costly reckoning.
about_author: Hazel Montrose is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing small-town records across the mountain West before turning to fiction. She writes about the people history files under 'miscellaneous,' and the machines they trust with their truths.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Elodie, proud of her invisibility in her master's workshop, is dispatched to Verenchal when the observatory's master clock stalls. POV: Elodie. Beat: reluctant departure; her belief that history belongs to other people established through her careful, unremarked craftsmanship.

chapters.title: Bridge Out at Verenchal
chapters.summary: The flood takes the bridge behind her carriage; Elodie is stranded for the season in a town that regards her with polite suspicion. She lodges with postmistress Ada Quill, who reads every letter that passes through. POV: Elodie. Beat: displacement, claustrophobia, first flicker of curiosity about the town's silences.

chapters.title: What the Clock Counts
chapters.summary: Repairing the master clock, Elodie finds a second, hidden ledger inside its case — names, dates, and payments from 1849 that don't match the town's official founding story. POV: Elodie. Beat: intrigue; the first crack in her conviction that she can remain a bystander.

chapters.title: The Kettle Creek Names
chapters.summary: Ada reveals the ledger records the erasure of Kettle Creek, a settlement drowned out and bought off, its families scattered. Schoolteacher Bram Ostley, fired for asking questions, joins them. POV: Elodie with Ada's oral testimony woven in. Beat: the personal becomes political; found family begins to form.

chapters.title: Centennial Preparations
chapters.summary: The founding families, led by judge Ambrose Hale, launch a grand centennial history to be sealed in the state archive on New Year's Eve. Elodie is offered a lucrative contract to restore the observatory for the ceremony — and to stay quiet. POV: Elodie. Beat: temptation and threat entwined; stakes made explicit.

chapters.title: The Clockmaker's Daughter
chapters.summary: Marguerite Vasseur, daughter of the clock's original maker, arrives claiming her father's ledger proves he was paid to hide the Kettle Creek evidence inside the mechanism. Her arrival splits the alliance — is she ally or Hale's informant? POV: Marguerite. Beat: distrust, grief, the cost of inherited complicity.

chapters.title: A Machine for Testimony
chapters.summary: In Ada's back room, the group assembles their counter-record on a battered typewriter: affidavits, the hidden ledger, Kettle Creek descendants' letters. Hale's men search the post office. POV: Bram. Beat: rising tension; the act of documentation becomes an act of courage.

chapters.title: The Longest Night
chapters.summary: Their draft is stolen and Ada is arrested on trumped-up charges of mail tampering. Elodie realizes the original ledger pages were never in the stolen draft — they are inside the clock, where she alone can reach them. POV: Elodie. Beat: despair turning to resolve; the climax's engine set.

chapters.title: Midnight, the Master Clock
chapters.summary: At the centennial ceremony, as Hale unveils the official history, Elodie triggers the repaired clock's chime mechanism to release the hidden pages over the assembled town, while Marguerite reads Kettle Creek's names aloud. POV: Elodie and Marguerite alternating. Beat: climax — truth spoken in public, at the exact turn of the century.

chapters.title: A New Reckoning of Hours
chapters.summary: The town, shamed but not destroyed, votes to amend its record and restore Kettle Creek's name to the valley map. Ada is freed; Elodie is offered the observatory post and, for the first time, chooses to stay. POV: Elodie. Beat: resolution — belonging earned not by hiding but by witness.
